state.task: Review a proposed CanLang language design; implementation is outside this consultation. The user asks to place translations beside their source text when possible, after meaningful # descriptions became less readable when replaced by abstract #= keys. Prioritize adoption, few tokens and lines, a single canonical mechanism, and accurate business meaning. A # line carries declaration description metadata, whereas ## marks a discarded comment. Mandatory catalogs originated with the assistant and were never imposed by the user. Novelty and brevity alone must not make an alternative preferable.
state.audit: An analysis scoped to AST ownership examined 44 sources and counted 724 named message rows. Of these, 699 are used once and 25 are used twice. The 373 messages used as descriptions all take no parameters, occur at exactly one use site, and have no additional reference. Moving those descriptions inline could eliminate 48 imports used only for descriptions, saving 1720 Unicode characters when newlines are counted. Generated labels occupy 1521 rows for 1892 targets. Grouping in 256 rows shares translations across 371 additional targets that would otherwise repeat them. Eighteen bindings for labels obtain their text from named messages. Two exported words are reused between owners. One typed ICU plural message also has multiple use sites. For the same CanDo excerpt, a proposed inline form changes the size from 42 physical lines to 32 and from 2344 Unicode characters to 2081. Model-token reductions were not measured. This inventory describes the source arrangement; it establishes neither semantic validity nor executable behavior.
state.research: IntlMessageFormat from FormatJS can format a supplied message string or an already parsed AST, so ICU formatting does not require keys authored in a catalog (https://formatjs.github.io/docs/intl-messageformat/). The ICU guidance favors translating complete messages and using explicit placeholders so languages can reorder grammar (https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/messages/). Fluent describes reusable terms while explaining constraints imposed by grammatical context (https://projectfluent.org/fluent/guide/terms.html). The references demonstrate possibilities for formatting and sharing; they do not choose CanLang syntax.
state.existing: In the current language, each owner specifies en,nl columns once in a messages table. That table contains named messages with typed inputs and bindings from generated-label targets to messages. The #= form is limited to a message path with no arguments and static content. Plain # descriptions and ordinary string expressions are literal text. Expression lists already use commas as separators. The token | forms named-type unions and has no expression-operator role. Caption attributes cannot currently be embedded on fields, parameters, enum cases or generated CRUD controls. A composed app may lack a Given section entirely; today its description obtains a message through an import from a different owner. Only syntax parsing exists: semantic checking for messages, an ICU engine, a renderer, a compiler and execution of BDD examples are absent.
state.common_contract: Every inline direction must use the same message-value form across descriptions, captions, UI text and human-directed outbound content. Supply canonical label locations on declarations, or beside controls owned by that declaration when no written declaration exists for the control. Existing bounded runtime vocabulary defaults and caption inheritance through schemas/types must remain implicit. Author names and exports only where a message is actually reused, and retain grouped bindings or an equivalent sharing facility so 371 labels are not copied. Plural forms and placeholders require explicitly bound, validated typed arguments; reusable named ICU declarations already retain that boundary. Being represented by strings must never automatically localize fixture text, ordinary business data, identifiers or routes. Assets derived by the compiler from owner/slot locations can feed both browser and MCP without author-supplied keys, while operation and schema machine identities remain unchanged. Putting content inline supplies no evidence by itself of locale completeness, correct ICU, permissions or functioning runtime behavior.
state.tradeoffs: With a source-text suffix, readable originals stay where they are used and translations carry explicit language tags. The cost is recurring tags, a way to escape reserved markers, and a source-language policy separate from the deployment default. One possible but undecided policy pins English as source and allows another source language through an explicit owner override. Bundles keyed for every variant also repeat language tags and require quoted description text, in return for local identification of all languages. Position-based variants avoid recurring tags, but any column-order or column-count change requires updates to all values. Their locale header must apply to the logical owner, including composed apps, rather than inheriting unintended file or deployment scope. Named tables as used today make review by locale centralized, expose explicit asset identities and enable reuse; for prose used once they add names, references and imports. All spellings illustrated here lack implementation, and neither their exact punctuation nor grammar for caption locations has been resolved.

feasible.instructions: Assuming the absent grammar, semantic checks and runtime behavior are implemented, can static declaration descriptions and messages used once be authored directly at their use sites without losing the given typing, reuse or machine-identity constraints? Evaluate whether the design can be built; do not assess whether the current parser already accepts it or regard feasibility as evidence that entire apps work.

placement.instructions: Considering independent ownership of sources, association of variants with languages and genuine reuse, which form most closely serves the user’s desire for readable inline text with less repetition? Balance every stated advantage against its stated cost. Choose unresolved when the evidence does not justify favoring a form. The choice concerns an overall direction and does not approve exact syntax that has yet to be finished.

criteria.suffix: Attach language-keyed translations to source prose/text written at the use site, using names only when reuse is real. In exchange for keeping originals readable locally and allowing locale additions independently, take on repeated tags, a source-language contract and escaping/reserved-marker design.
criteria.keyed: Write a bundle inline with an explicit language key for the source as well as each translation, preserving assets needed for actual sharing. Self-contained language identity avoids column ordering and an implied source locale, at the cost of recurring tags and putting description prose in quotes.
criteria.positional: Use ordered variants at each site after specifying language columns once for its logical owner; keep names for truly shared messages. Reducing repeated language tags requires coordinated edits when columns change and a header contract that also works for composed apps.
criteria.named: Keep all translatable content in mandatory named table rows and refer to those rows at each site. The existing reuse model, review of grouped locales and author-chosen asset names come with indirection for one-use text and imports for metadata.
criteria.unresolved: Decline to choose a form when outstanding contracts for source language, label locations or ownership leave insufficient grounds to prefer one of the supplied directions.
